subject: Discovery Recap: Multi-tenancy controls (rate limits, quotas, per-customer routing)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Hunter <sam.hunter@fintechco.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@payments.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery Recap: Multi-tenancy controls (rate limits, quotas, per-customer routing)

Hi Sam and Priya  thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so everyone has the same notes and next steps. Please reply with any corrections or additions.

What we heard (pain points)
- Unpredictable token costs across customers; need per-customer quotaing to avoid runaway spend.
- Need rate limits and burst controls per customer for spikes (particularly around batch invoice processing).
- Desire for per-customer routing/policies: premium customers should hit higher-throughput pool / lower-latency models, while lower tiers use cost-optimized variants.
- Auditability: they must be able to show per-customer usage and logs for compliance and chargeback.

Current stack / constraints
- FinTechCo runs primary app on AWS us-west-2, uses internal API gateway and a multi-tenant Postgres instance.
- Currently proxying requests to a generic inference endpoint; no per-customer isolation or quotas today.
- Security: SOC2 in progress  any solution must support audit logs and integrate with their SIEM.

Success criteria (what would success look like in 90 days)
1) Enforceable per-customer quotas and rate limits that prevent overage events.
2) Per-customer routing policies mapped to billing tiers.
3) Visibility: token-level breakdown per customer + exportable logs for audits.

Proposed next steps
- Share a draft rate_limits_matrix.xlsx with suggested quota defaults (attached).
- Schedule a 60-min technical deep dive (integration + routing) with your infra team next week.
- Provide a short mutual action plan doc for procurement and security (link below).

Attachments: rate_limits_matrix.xlsx, redwood-multi-tenant-overview.pdf
Related link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1MA-action-plan

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0182

From: Sam Hunter <sam.hunter@fintechco.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@payments.io>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Multi-tenancy controls (rate limits, quotas, per-customer routing)

Thanks Ben  this looks accurate. Couple of quick clarifications:
- For quotas: we prefer soft limits with alerting + hard caps that block calls only for the very highest tier.
- For routing: premium customers should have a guaranteed slice of capacity; is there a way to define both shared and reserved pools?

We'll pull in our infra lead (cc'd in follow-up) for the technical deep dive  Thursday or Friday next week works.

Sam
Director of Engineering
FinTechCo

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Hunter <sam.hunter@fintechco.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@payments.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Multi-tenancy controls (rate limits, quotas, per-customer routing)

Appreciate the clarifications, Sam  helpful. Quick responses inline: 
- Soft + hard limits: yes, Redwood supports layered quota policies (alerts at soft threshold, enforce at hard cap). We'll surface breach events to your SIEM and can trigger webhooks.
- Shared + reserved pools: supported. We can provision reserved capacity for premium customers and route via customer attributes; remaining traffic hits a shared, cost-optimized pool.

I scheduled the technical deep dive for Thursday 2026-06-18 at 10:00 AM PT  invite sent to your infra team separately.

Action items for FinTechCo:
- Share a list of 10 pilot customers (IDs) and their expected qps/token budgets.
- Confirm compliance contact for log ingestion and SOC2 artifact requests.

Attached is a draft rate_limits_matrix.xlsx with suggested starting values; Marissa will run through recommended defaults in the tech call.

Link to mutual action plan: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1MA-action-plan

Best,
Ben
